question.text: Mr. Sameer Joshi, Head of Fund Operations at Yamuna Cat I VC Fund (2019 vintage), is asked by an institutional LP: 'Where does your 18% Net IRR rank versus peer 2019-vintage India VC funds?' Per Section 10.8 and SEBI's benchmarking-agency framework, which approach is MOST appropriate for Cat I/II AIFs?

answer.text: Benchmark the fund against NIFTY 50 price return (no TRI) on a point-to-point basis across fund tenure.

Use vintage-year peer benchmarking — compare the fund's pooled IRR, TVPI, DPI, and RVPI against the database of 2019-vintage India Cat I AIFs maintained by a SEBI-recognised Benchmarking Agency (CRISIL, NSE, Preqin), and report the peer quartile.
Benchmark against a fixed hurdle rate such as 10% p.a. with no peer comparison, as vintage-year matching is not required under SEBI rules.
Use the Sensex 30 as the sole benchmark since Cat I funds predominantly invest in Indian equities.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 10.8 and 10.8.1, SEBI (Circulars Feb 6, 2020 and Jun 12, 2020) mandated benchmarking agencies to build vintage-year peer benchmarks for Cat I/II AIFs using pooled IRR, investment multiples, DPI, RVPI, and TVPI. Three agencies are appointed via IVCA — CRISIL, NSE, Preqin. Reporting is half-yearly (as on Sep 30 / Mar 31). **The Trap:** Option A uses point-to-point equity return, which is cash-flow blind. Option C describes the Cat III 'absolute return' strategy — NOT Cat I/II. Option D applies a broad-based equity index to early-stage illiquid investments. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests the existence of benchmarking agencies for distributor conversations. XIX-C tests mechanics: vintage, pooled IRR, DPI/RVPI/TVPI, half-yearly reporting. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Request your Benchmark Report from CRISIL/NSE/Preqin ON TIME — SEBI Sep 19, 2024 circular gives you 7 months after FY-end. Missing the deadline bars you from stating 'peer 1st quartile' in marketing material, which is a fundraising killer for your next fund.
